results.summary_before: This is a custom high-density shift register implemented as an analog/transistor-level block, with 8 serial inputs, 8 serial outputs, and two clock phases. The documentation is essentially a placeholder, with the how-it-works, how-to-test, and external-hardware sections all left as FIXME. Silicon test reports from the author and an independent tester indicate that shift-register behavior was observed for both the internal-clock and dual-phase-clock variants, with data emerging roughly 36 cycles later, though the micropython-driven timings are described as unreliable. The notable point is that the custom cell works in silicon despite the minimal documentation.

results.summary_before: This design, called "Tiny tapeouts test gates", displays the letter H on a BCD display when all inputs are set to 1. It uses inverters on two pins to change their values from 1 to 0, forming the pattern needed for the letter H on a seven-segment display. The output pins are configured to drive the display segments, with specific pins set high or low; for example, OUT0 and OUT3 are 0 while others are 1. The project is a simple test of logic gates and display driving, requiring a seven-segment display as external hardware.
